We will provide materials, but if you have any meaningful or interesting objects you'd like to try making prints with, feel free to bring them along! Are you interested in learning new crafts? Working on setting and meeting new goals? Meeting other like-minded people and making new friends? Welcome to the Crafters Society! The Crafters Society is a new, monthly craft club specifically aimed at adults between the ages of 18-35 who are interested in flexing their creative muscles, setting new goals, and looking to approach life more mindfully. item.title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting — Mon Jul 27, 9:30 AM — Church of the Nazarene (a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted)
item.description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.
In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.
Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.
We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA (a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted) and newcomers are always welcome.
You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html
OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.
Members have different plans of eating.
OA does not endorse any specific food plan.
Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/
Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.or

item.title: Discussion: What is a Just War? — Wed Jul 29, 5:30 PM — St. Columba's Inverness
item.description:
In a time when our nation is engaged in multiple conflicts using warfare, how do we discern what is just and what is not?
St. Columba’s Inverness Social Justice Ministry is sponsoring What Is a Just War?, a community discussion exploring the Anglican Communion’s Just War principles. These timeless guidelines can help us understand today's news and inspire faithful, constructive responses.
All are invited. All perspectives are welcome.
The event takes place Wednesday, July 29, from 5:30 to 6:30 p.m. at St. Columba’s Inverness, 12835 Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Inverness.
Get more information about the Social Justice Ministry and more at stcolumbasinverness.org

item.title: Soul Motion®: Body Prayer every Sunday in person — Sun Aug 2, 10:00 AM — Wischemann Hall
item.description: BODY PRAYER IS A FACILITATED EVENT DEVOTED TO INQUIRY INTO EMBODIED CONSCIOUSNESS THROUGH MOVEMENT. This class is offered every Sunday morning, and led by Zuza Engler or another teacher. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. What to expect Guidance and structure are part of every week’s class as we travel across the four landscapes of Soul Motion®: Dance Infinite (prayer space) Dance Community (ensemble) Dance Communion (duet) Dance Intimate (solo) Practices, structures, and points of view are offered to facilitate the journey. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance. We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html
In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

item.title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour — Sat Aug 22, 10:00 AM — The Floathouse Petaluma
item.description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”
Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.
